name: Congenital Hypothalamic Hamartoma Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Hypothalamic Hamartoma Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of gelastic seizures characterized by inappropriate bouts of laughter
Identification of hypothalamic hamartoma on MRI
Evidence of central precocious puberty onset before age 8 in females or 9 in males
Presence of cognitive impairment or behavioral disturbances including aggression or developmental delay

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of gelastic seizures and MRI-confirmed hypothalamic hamartoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Precocious puberty and cognitive/behavioral symptoms support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

searchTerms: benign hypothalamic brain mass on MRI

common.symptomName: Behavioral disturbances including aggression and irritability

occasional.symptomName: Other seizure types (tonic, atonic, or complex partial seizures)
searchTerms: other seizure types like tonic or complex
weight gain due to hypothalamic issues

rare.symptomName: Visual field defects due to mass effect
searchTerms: vision loss due to brain mass effect
visual field loss from tumor pressure
partial blindness from mass pressing on optic pathways

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to CSF flow obstruction
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain from blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow

laboratory: Elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in precocious puberty
Increased testosterone or estradiol levels depending on sex and pubertal status
imaging: MRI showing non-enhancing, isointense hypothalamic mass consistent with hamartoma
No surrounding edema or mass effect in typical cases
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; usually sporadic
other: EEG abnormalities corresponding to gelastic seizures

distinguishingFeatures: MRI shows enhancing tumor mass with infiltrative features
Other CNS lesions identified on imaging
Different clinical presentation depending on lesion type
MRI abnormalities localized to temporal lobe

redFlags: Onset of gelastic seizures in infancy or early childhood
Rapid progression of cognitive decline or behavioral disturbances
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as vomiting or papilledema
references: Delalande O, Fohlen M. Hypothalamic hamartomas and epilepsy. Epilepsia. 2011;52 Suppl 8:19-24.
Ng YT, Rekate HL, Prenger EC, et al. Hypothalamic hamartomas: clinical features and surgical treatment. Neurosurg Focus. 2007;23(2):E9.
Orphanet: Congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
